I regard education as a transformative process: one that shares knowledge on
one side and inspires curiosity, a passion for learning, and critical thinking
on the other. Good teaching is reciprocal — a constructive and respectful
exchange between students and instructor, built on mutual trust.

I am a committed advocate of active learning. Rather than have students
passively receive content, I build my courses around group discussion, case
studies drawn from the primary literature, problem-solving exercises, and
hands-on work. This comes naturally in my field: ecology is a quantitative,
data-rich science, and I want students to move confidently from field
observations and raw data to inference — and to do so reproducibly. In
practice that means teaching not only ecological concepts but the
computational and statistical literacy that modern ecology demands, so
students leave able to analyse their own data.

I have taught in both English and Italian, and all of my teaching can be
delivered in English.

## Supervision

I have supervised and mentored more than ten bachelor's, master's and doctoral
candidates. Many are co-authors on our joint publications, which reflects how I
approach supervision: students work on real questions, with real data, and the
output is real science. Recent completions:

::: {.teach-list}

Mississippi State University and the University of Leeds.

## Teaching material

I am a strong advocate of accessible knowledge. I build course material online
and make it freely available to my students, in open course companions where
they can review material, download slides, and find the references discussed in
class.

- [**Animal Tracking in Conservation Biology**](https://giulianocolosimo.github.io/animtrack-2627/) — the full course
  companion: session-by-session material, the R exercises, and the schedule.
- [**Conservation Biology**](biocon.qmd) — course outline, topics covered, and
  the reading list.

I co-authored *Un Viaggio nell'ambiente R* (Russo, **Colosimo**, et al.,
University of Rome Tor Vergata Publishing Service, 2026), a textbook for
students meeting the R programming environment for the first time. I curated
the chapter on using R for the analysis of genetic and genomic data. It is
listed on the [publications](publications.qmd) page.
